originality.rationale: The covariance is already in arxiv:2401.07972 Eq. (28), and noisy Gaussian AR1 inverse-covariance behavior is standard; neither is presented as a discovery. The new finding is the unique global thermal-parameter maximizer of every nonadjacent all-other-velocities-conditioned pair information, increasing optimizer temperatures, and coefficient-sharp large-distance law. Primary full-text comparisons of arxiv:2401.07972, 2402.11358 and 1809.09931 show no statement or dominating implication giving that classification. A 2016 Gaussian prediction-information study is only abstract-accessible and remains a recognized novelty risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Chavez (2016) was not accessible; only its abstract and citation metadata could be assessed.
Some older Gaussian time-series/moving-average results may imply a noisily parametrized special case indirectly, although targeted searches found no equivalent temperature-optimization theorem.

The physics source establishes the covariance exactly; the new claim is a derived stationary information theorem, not a new dynamical model. Independent literature-priority validation remains unperformed.

value.rationale: The natural information between two velocities after conditioning on all other velocities is not determined by ordinary pair correlation alone: adding thermal noise changes the spatial Gaussian Markov graph, and each nonadjacent pair has a unique nonzero information optimum. The full family of sharp temperatures, their strict ordering and the universal geometric-over-linear asymptotic quantify a meaningful noise-assisted spatial-information effect in a physical model, beyond a routine fixed-n calculation.
